status: open release-blocking finding for the PP.4 Core matrix

runtime.artifact_verified: public Sigstore-verified rc.23 install on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 KVM guest

discovered_by: campaign phase 9 (cross-interface lifecycle deletion) feeding phase 10 (TestLab teardown + reset contract)

harness.note: phases 7-9 of this harness pass; the defect is in the product's delete path, not in the harness

defect_1_native_delete_leaves_the_port.summary: Deleting a compatibility-created server through the native interface marks the server resource DELETED but leaves its auto-created port ACTIVE. The mirror-image path (native-created server deleted through the compatibility interface) releases its port correctly, so the two interfaces leave different durable state for the same logical operation.
observed_sequence: phase 4: `openstack server create` -> O3K server 03ea1326-677c-55a2-b150-24e7d0fb2301 (name pp4-openstack), O3K auto-creates port 01a0c9b2-55bb-71e3-a07a-26ba9a36eb44 (o3k-server:<project>:pp4-openstack, 192.0.2.4)
phase 9: native `DELETE /o3k/v1/compute/servers/03ea1326-...` succeeds; the campaign then asserts the server is invisible through the compatibility interface -> PASS

durable state after the delete: compute_instance 03ea1326-... desired_state=DELETED, observed_state=DELETED (provider domain o3k-1028c71a9088417cb96d), but network_ports still holds 01a0c9b2-... status ACTIVE
control case: native-created server 009c1501-... (pp4-native) deleted through the compatibility interface -> its port bdd0c9be-... is gone
consequence: the shipped teardown cannot remove the subnet: `openstack subnet delete testlab-subnet` -> 409 Conflict 'network operation is not allowed'
bootstrap-testlab.sh --teardown aborts: 'TestLab bootstrap failed: subnet deletion was not verified: testlab-subnet'
campaign phase 10 fails ('FAIL TestLab teardown failed (before-reset)'), so the required reset / uninstall / purge and reinstall steps cannot run
the orphaned ACTIVE port also blocks a follow-up create on the same subnet

defect_2_failed_create_leaves_an_error_r.summary: A server create that fails with 'compute operation conflicts with current state (HTTP 409)' leaves a compute_instance resource in observed_state ERROR plus an ACTIVE port behind, i.e. the rollback path does not release the port it allocated.
observed_sequence: the follow-up reproduction attempted `openstack server create --flavor testlab-flavor --image cirros-0.6.3 --network testlab-network --wait leak-repro`
result: 'compute operation conflicts with current state (HTTP 409)'
durable state afterwards: compute_instance d1ff174c-81b5-541e-a37b-84160e8cdc40 observed_state=ERROR with network_ids ['01a0c9b9-ee17-7c53-8c09-e02b0426be3e'], and that port exists ACTIVE (192.0.2.2)
defect_2_failed_create_leaves_an_error_r.note: recorded as a distinct cleanup/rollback gap; it is the same class of leak but on the failure path rather than the delete path

classification.candidate_verdict: v0.4.0-rc.23 is a FAILED immutable PP.4 candidate: the required cross-interface delete -> teardown -> reset/uninstall/purge matrix cannot complete
classification.not_a_harness_defect: the harness assertions passed exactly what the product reported (server gone through both interfaces); the inconsistency is in the durable state the product keeps
classification.not_a_compatibility_profile_change: no public API surface changes are required by the fix; this is resource cleanup/rollback correctness in the native delete path
classification.debian_not_run: per the campaign rule, Debian is not started while a product defect blocks Ubuntu

required_fix: make the native server delete release the same auto-created port that the compatibility delete releases, so both interfaces converge on identical durable state
make a failed create roll back the port it allocated instead of leaving an ERROR resource plus an ACTIVE port

regression tests: native delete of a compat-created server releases its port; compat delete of a native-created server releases its port; a failed create releases its port and its address allocation; a server delete unblocks subnet deletion (the teardown precondition)
open_questions: whether the port is meant to be released synchronously with the delete operation or by a bounded reconciler pass, and which of the two the contract requires
whether the create failure path's ERROR resource is intended to be terminal evidence or should be compensated
